Afterwards a second, optional scan — with glasses, different facial hair or other lighting — makes recognition even more reliable at any time of day.

Snapshots of your face that Ubuntu Hello compares against. Keep at least two, recorded in different lighting.

Only one face model is enrolled. Glasses, a change of facial hair or different lighting change how your face looks to the camera, so a single model can fail (for example in the evening under lamps). Add a second model with glasses on or off, your other look, or in different light to keep unlocking reliable.

Enable face authentication to automatically unlock your login keyring or KWallet on login. This securely stores your password sealed in the TPM when available, or encrypted with AES-256-GCM using a root-only master key. Face auth sets PAM_AUTHTOK for pam_gnome_keyring or pam_kwallet5 depending on your desktop.

We're done! Ubuntu Hello is now active on this computer. Try doing anything you would normally have to type your password for to authenticate, like running a command with sudo. If you enabled keyring auto-unlock, your login keyring or KWallet will also be unlocked automatically on login.

You can open the Ubuntu Hello Configurator later on to change more advanced settings or add additional models. Press Finish below to close this window and open the Ubuntu Hello Configurator.
Because of changes in angles, distance, and other factors a face match is never exactly the same as the stored face model. On this page you can set how strict Ubuntu Hello should be.
The most forgiving match and the quickest to let you in. Choose this if convenience matters more than strictness.
A strict match that still logs you in quickly. It may not recognise you at a sharp angle or from further away.
The strictest match, with no extra step when you log in. Recommended.
You can add more face models later from Settings or with: sudo ubuntu-hello add
Look at the camera you selected: an infrared camera shows a small light that blinks while Ubuntu Hello tests it. This tells us whether it can see your face in the dark.

Ubuntu Hello will search your system automatically for any available cameras, so make sure your webcam is connected. After detection a list of usable webcams will be shown. Pick the one you want to use and click Next.
Ubuntu Hello needs three pre trained facial recognition datasets to be able to recognise you, which will be downloaded now. You can see the download progress below.
